key_insight: An interpretable hybrid model encoded the Alzheimer's A/T/N biomarker framework as logic rules while using neural networks to extract biomarker features, improving adaptable incident AD prediction.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier Alzheimer's risk stratification years before symptoms by combining biomarker-based staging with more transparent model reasoning.
method: Logic-programmed the A/T/N framework for interpretability
Used neural networks to learn biomarker features for the rule-based model
Estimated relative importance scores for A/T/N profiles
evidence_signal: In the ADNI dataset, the pipeline predicted four-year incident AD with sensitivity up to 0.84 and suggested existing A and T cutoffs may not generalize well.
watch_item: The findings are based on one dataset and a specific biomarker framework, so performance and cutoff validity may not transfer directly without external validation.
paper_title: Encoding Discordance in the Alzheimer's Disease A/T/N Framework
